newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sentrachem, Hoechst commission plant.
newsitem.headline: Sentrachem, Hoechst commission plant.

text.p: South African chemical firms Sentrachem Ltd and Hoechst South Africa Ltd said on Tuesday the 235 million rand expansion project for the manufacture of polypropylene had been commissioned on schedule.

The project is based at Safripol, a firm jointly owned by Sentrachem and Hoechst which have during the past seven years invested almost 400 million rand in the expansion of its polypropylene and polyethylene manufacturing capacity.
At the same time the firms announced a 20 million rand expansion of the high density polyethylene plant at Safripol, which will increase capacity by 20,000 tonnes a year to 180,000 tonnes.
The plant is scheduled for completion towards the end of this year.
The 235 million rand investment in the polypropylene plant, which was opened on Tuesday, will increase capacity to 90,000 tonnes per annum from 55,000 currently, the firms said.
The increased capacity would be used to continue servicing Safripol's domestic market.

However, once the plant was fully operational, Plastomark, a joint marketing venture between Sentrachem and Hoechst, plans to export between 25,000 and 30,000 tonnes a year to Africa, the Far East and other selected markets.

Together with existing exports of high density polyethylene worth around 70 million rand, also marketed by Plastomark, this would push total export earnings per annum to 160 million at current exchange rates.
The firms said polypropylene is recognised as one of the most versatile plastics and is used in the manufacture of products including carpets, ropes, automotive parts and pipes.
Demand worldwide, and in South Africa, has been rising at between eight and 10 percent a year.
High density polyethylene is used for the manufacture of packaging film, crates and bottles with domestic demand for these products growing rapidly, they said.
